context: Dispatched to scope visit cancellation into a new requirement under Visits. The distillate settles the semantics: hard delete, upcoming visits only, owner detail page. It does not address the PRD Non-Goals table. NG-4 covers deleting an owner, a pet, or a visit. NG-5 covers changing or cancelling a visit once booked. Both were confirmed deliberate on 2026-08-08 by adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. That ADR states a future request touching either row proceeds only on an explicit owner decision recorded at intake, and that the request itself never reopens the row. No such decision appears in the distillate, so I stopped before drafting. Ledger note: the dispatch-start at line 1 stamped REQ-VIS-002, an ID already in use for showing earlier visits during booking. Line 2 supersedes it with REQ-VIS-003.
question: Do you decide to narrow NG-4 and NG-5 so cancelling an upcoming visit becomes in scope? I recommend narrowing rather than withdrawing. NG-4 would keep owner and pet deletion out and open visit removal only. NG-5 would keep amendment and any cancelled-status lifecycle out and open removal of an upcoming visit only. A hard delete adds no lifecycle state, so the ADR's stated reason for NG-5 survives that narrowing. On your confirmation I will record the narrowing in a non-goal ADR, amend both rows, and scope REQ-VIS-003 with acceptance criteria. If you decline, the request stops here.
stop_state: docs/prd.md and docs/ubiquitous-language.md unedited. REQ-VIS-003 minted, not drafted. Awaiting the boundary decision before writing any requirement.
